editorial:
Imagine you are traveling back to 1973 for a family funeral in the South. You meet Uncle Frank, who seems like the cool, open-minded relative compared to the rest of your strict family. He takes his niece, Beth, on a long road trip from New York to South Carolina. Along the way, they are joined by Frank's partner, Walid. The vibe starts off as a cozy, coming-of-age story about a young woman discovering who she is while learning about love and honesty from her favorite uncle.

The acting is really solid, and the chemistry between the leads makes you care about them. However, be ready for a huge shift in the mood halfway through that changes everything you thought you knew about Frank. It is a bold choice that might feel jarring, but it makes the story memorable. If you enjoy dramas with big surprises, you should definitely check this out. You can rent it on Apple TV for a quick watch, or if you want the best picture quality, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is the way to go.
endingExplained: The big twist reveals that Frank is actually a dangerous con artist who uses his charm to steal money from people. He is not the saint Beth thought he was. By the end, Frank's lies catch up to him, and he ends up in a bad situation. Beth finally sees him for who he really is and chooses to walk away from his toxic influence to start her own honest life.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves character studies and surprise plot twists.
